feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Evidence from earlier races: iteration 5 (five sensors at x ±0.04 m, y 0.06 m, 12 mm footprints, kp 3.5, kd 0.6) scored 465.8, the best so far, with oval finish 0.95, s-bend finish 0.20, s-bend line loss 0.95 and s-bend max_error 0.0591 m. Iteration 6 widened the span to ±0.05 m at y 0.06 m: s-bend line loss fell to 0.65 and max_error held at 0.0599 m, but the oval fell to 0.90 and the score to 449.9. Iteration 7 (±0.05 m, y 0.07 m) gave oval 1.00 but s-bend max_error 0.0626 m and s-bend finish 0. Iteration 8 interpolated (±0.045 m, y 0.065 m) and scored 432.4, with s-bend line loss 1.0 and max_error 0.0619 m, so moving the forward offset off y 0.06 m hurt. Iteration 1 showed that widening coverage cut line loss without adding completions. For the footprint change, I hold the sensor pitch at 0.02 m, so the 16 mm footprint extends each sensor's reach across the tape edge without moving the row, and I keep the Iteration 5 controller (kp 3.5, kd 0.6) because the weight scale is unchanged. Read the next race as follows. If s-bend line loss falls below 0.9 with max_error at or below 0.06 m and the oval stays at 0.95, keep the 16 mm footprint and test a narrower outer step. If s-bend line loss stays near 0.95 with no oval or max_error change, the footprint is not the lever, so return to 12 mm and hand the remaining s-bend problem to the controller side.
requested_changes: If s-bend line_loss_events falls below 0.9 with s-bend max_error at or below 0.06 m and oval finish holding at 0.95, keep sensor_size 0.016 m and try outer sensors at x = ±0.045 m with y = 0.06 m (not y 0.065). Evidence: iteration 6 (±0.05 m) cut s-bend line loss from 0.95 to 0.65, but iteration 8 (y 0.065, ±0.045 m) scored 432.4, so keep y at 0.06 m.

If s-bend line_loss_events stays near 0.95 with max_error near 0.059 m and the oval finish unchanged, return sensor_size to 0.012 m. Evidence: iteration 5 (12 mm) and this footprint change share the same span and forward offset, so a footprint-only change that does not cut line loss is not the lever.

If the oval finish drops below 0.95 with steering_oscillation above about 0.30 on the oval, return sensor_size to 0.012 m and keep ±0.04 m. Evidence: iteration 6 showed the wider span cost the oval (0.95 to 0.90), and iteration 5 at 12 mm held 0.95.
